entry: Synthetic worked example - not empirical evidence and not reusable as a result
Sensitivity of API admission-control policies under bursty synthetic workloads
Under declared arrival, service and burst assumptions, how do token-bucket and fixed-window policies differ in false rejection, admitted load, queue-tail behaviour and overflow risk?
One simulation scenario defined by policy, offered load, burst factor, service distribution and random seed.
Synthetic discrete-event simulation; one service pool; no production traffic, user data or deployment claim.
Token-bucket versus fixed-window, checked against hand-calculated limiting cases and a no-control reference.
Token-bucket control is superior for production APIs.
